title: scope.request/1
description: One per observed request: the sensor's record. Attribute names follow the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where one exists (http.*, url.*, server.*, user_agent.original, network.*, tls.*, mcp.*); the rest live under scope.*. Exported as an OTLP log record with event_name scope.request. Additive changes stay in this major; a field's meaning never changes; removal is a new major.

hash12.description: sha256(salt + ':' + value)[0:12]; a join key inside the salt epoch, nothing else

reference.description: eight base32 characters: three minting-minute characters, four random, one check

prefixedId.description: a prefixed, opaque id minted by Scope; records themselves carry a UUIDv7 and no prefix

id.description: UUIDv7 minted by the sensor; the record's identity and its idempotency key at the ingest

ts.description: when the request arrived at the sensor

observed_ts.description: when the record was complete (after the response went out; at the end of a stream)

install.description: the install this sensor runs as; null only on a sensor with no install id (a lab deployment)

source.description: the form of the sensor that recorded this

package.description: the npm package of the adapter

version.description: the package version (every package takes one version)

adapter.description: cloudflare, next, node, envoy, drain-vercel, drain-cloudflare

policy_version.description: the policy version the sensor ran this request under; 0 is the embedded forward-only default

salt_epoch.description: the customer's salt epoch the hashes were made in; hashes never join across epochs

request_id.description: the platform's own request id (cf-ray, x-vercel-id, x-amz-cf-id): the one key a connector's record and a sensor's record share

server.address.description: the host the agent spoke to (the sensor's), which is also a signature's authority

url.path.description: redacted like url.query (a secret-named pair's value, and a segment holding an encoded pair from its start, become h:<hash>), then by shape: a value of the product's signed shape is replaced by its hash

url.query.description: the query string without the leading question mark; the value of a secret-named parameter (api_key, key, token, access_token, refresh_token, id_token, code, client_secret, password, secret, signature, sig, session_id, in any case or spelling, also percent-encoded, or a name whose last word is key, token, secret, password, signature or sig, also inside a URL another parameter carries) becomes h:<hash>, unless it is a valid reference code where the policy says a reference travels (headers.reference, a door's fields.reference); a value that carries an encoded parameter of its own, or is still encoded after four decodings, becomes h:<hash> from the start of the path segment that holds it; a string holding more than 64 such values is recorded as one hash; then redacted by shape; null when the url has none

scope.route.description: the surface role of the path, from the policy's surface map

scope.request.bytes.description: the request body's size in bytes, when the body was read

scope.response.bytes.description: the response body's size, when the body was read or, for an event stream, counted as it passed (in bytes)

scope.cache.description: cf-cache-status or x-vercel-cache as seen on the origin's answer

origin_ms.description: the origin's answer time as seen from the sensor

total_ms.description: from arrival to the record's completion

scope.client.address_hash.description: a one-way hash of the client's address; the address itself never leaves

scope.client.address_family.description: so that a dual-stack client seen on two hosts can be read as such

scope.client.colo.description: the edge location that served the request

scope.client.fetch_metadata.description: the browser signals a fetcher does not send: how a browser is told from a tool

scope.client.ja4.description: the TLS client fingerprint when the platform exposes it

agent.description: the Signature-Agent header: the origin that publishes the signing key

valid.description: true only after the sensor verified the signature against the listed signer's key directory

reason.description: verified, expired, not_yet_valid, unknown_key, directory_unreachable, bad_signature, unsupported_alg, authority_mismatch, or unlisted_signer (a signer the policy's signers do not list; no directory is fetched)

authority.description: the host the signature covers and is verified against (the sensor's)

scope.platform_bot.description: the platform's verified-bot match, when the zone has bot management

scope.reader.description: the reader family, from the signature, the agent string, Accept and the fetch metadata; vendor-client is the customer's own CLI or SDK by the policy's clients patterns

scope.key.credential.description: the hashed bearer of the Authorization header; the value never leaves

scope.key.install.description: the hashed install id the policy's install header carried

scope.key.device_code.description: the hashed device code of a device-flow start or poll, when bodies are recorded

scope.key.user_code.description: the hashed user code of a device-flow start or approval, when bodies are recorded

scope.key.oauth_client.description: the hashed OAuth client id of a registration, authorization, approval or token call, when bodies are recorded (the authorize query is read in every form)

mcp.session.id.description: the hash of the MCP session id the request carried; the one the answer assigned is in scope.response.headers, hashed the same way

scope.key.hook.description: the id of a catch hook, from the catch path or the creation answer

scope.key.reference.description: the reference the request carried (query, setup header, body field named by the policy); only a value with the reference shape and check character counts, so another value in a reference parameter (a device user code in code= on a sign-in page) is not recorded here (the device door records it as scope.key.user_code)

scope.key.setup_header.description: the policy's setup header: a valid reference code as sent, any other value (the session id the gate hands out) hashed like mcp.session.id

scope.key.intent_header.description: the policy's intent header, redacted like url.query and by shape; a filled one is also a declaration

mcp.method.name.description: the JSON-RPC methods of the request's messages, in order; kept in every form

scope.mcp.tools.description: the tools the request called, in order; kept in every form

scope.mcp.client.description: the client the MCP handshake named; kept in every form

scope.oauth.description: what an OAuth call named about itself; kept in every form

scope.body.request.description: the request body on an observed route, parsed as JSON or a form (capped at 64 KB), cut to the fields observe.bodies.allow_fields names at any depth, with the values of the policy's secret fields and of the secret names (as in url.query; code only in a request) and the shapes hashed; null when no allowed field remains and in the no-bodies form

scope.body.response.description: the same for the origin's answer, also on an error answer (400 or above) from any route the surface map does not pass through; an event stream's content is never recorded, only its size in scope.response.bytes

scope.body.truncated.description: true when a body exceeded 64 KB and was cut before parsing

scope.response.headers.description: the answer headers the stitcher needs: content-type, mcp-session-id (hashed), www-authenticate, location (redacted like url.query), cache-control, x-vercel-cache, cf-cache-status

canonical.description: the page's path without a face suffix

reference_minted.description: the reference minted into this serve of the page, when an inject rule placed it

injected.description: the labels of the inject rules that changed the page

scope.page.description: present on a page read (a docs page, the root map, the helpful 404)

scope.reference_minted.description: a reference minted into a non-page answer (an error link, a finder answer); a page's reference, the helpful 404's included, is scope.page.reference_minted

scope.decision.description: what every rule that matched did, in rule order, and the observer's own steps as rules of kind observe: `policy` (the embedded default ran: errored, reason `built-in default: <why>`), `assertion` (the assertion could not be signed) and `hop` (the hop failed after the request may have left: answered 502, or 504 on a timeout, and not sent again)

scope.gateway.description: on the MCP route: how many messages the gate answered and how many it forwarded

scope.observer.errors.description: the sensor's own errors on this request, by class; the request was forwarded untouched

scope.observer.dropped.description: records the sensor failed to ship since its last successful shipment
